analysis.title: Nordic Alert: Anthropic revived stock markets, but shock in Brazil
key_insights: US and European stocks started the week in a better mood and oil has fallen slightly from recent highs. US stocks were boosted by news that Anthropic has applied for a Nasdaq listing.
Meta announced a planned new share issue of USD 95 billion to finance its AI investments.
Asian stocks are mixed: higher in Japan and IT-heavy Korea, lower in Shanghai. Stock futures point slightly up in the US and down in Europe.

Brazil's markets reacted with shock to Lula's unexpected election win over Flávio Bolsonaro. The currency fell close to 8% and the stock market about 14%. The concern is that Lula continues on a path of rising budget deficits and interest rates. Bolsonaro's party has recognized Lula as the winner.

Markets await interest rate announcements from almost all major central banks this week and next, plus the US midterm elections. Fed pricing has crept higher but still points to a very high probability of unchanged rates at tomorrow's meeting.

Betting odds and polls point to a Democratic win of all of Congress, with small margins in several key Senate races. A Democratic sweep would block Trump's fiscal agenda and new appointments, including to the Fed, but would not impede the White House much on foreign, immigration and trade policy.
Democrats' ability to pass their own policies would be limited by Trump's veto, and their initiatives would likely be tests of policy ahead of the 2028 presidential election.
The US and Canada are showing progress in trade talks. Trump eased some import tariffs to support Maine Republican Senator Susan Collins ahead of the midterms.

Today's agenda focuses on household well-being: consumer confidence in France and the US, plus US durable goods orders and housing data. French consumers may be affected by the recent sharp rise in bond yields and violent mass demonstrations.

US consumer sentiment stayed near lows in October per the Michigan index. The Conference Board index has held up better but has also fallen recently. SEB will watch the 'jobs plentiful' versus 'jobs hard to get' gap, which tends to correlate with unemployment.

Israel's general election is today. Most polls show the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot ahead of Netanyahu but short of the 61-seat Knesset majority, with Arab parties likely holding the swing vote. If no government forms, Israel may hold another election early next year with Netanyahu leading an interim government.

Per Israeli newspapers, the current IDF chief of staff opposed a Netanyahu request to attack Iran shortly before the election. According to CNN, Netanyahu also tried to get Trump to agree to a joint attack.
Riksbank: a November hike looks close to certain, but SEB thinks the market prices in too many hikes further ahead. Swedish consumer goods PPI rose less than expected yesterday.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fed pricing has crept higher with calmer markets but still points to no change at tomorrow's meeting.

Softer producer price pressure than forecast.
